Authors: Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (EDS) is a condition characterised by remarkably elastic and fragile skin with unusually flexible joints. The most common subtype of EDS, hyperplastic EDS (hEDS) arises from mutations in collagen-related genes, yet the specific mutation and its underlying mechanism remain elusive. We aim to elucidate the molecular underpinnings of the disease by studying the fibroblast extracellular matrices (ECM) and analysing the levels of different amino acids in collagen using solid-state Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (ssNMR).
